newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democratic camp suffers new split over 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK democratic camp suffers new split over 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp suffered a fresh blow on Wednesday when a member of the popular Democratic Party broke ranks and said he would apply to join a provisional legislature that China plans to install next year.
"The provisional legislature will be set up. It is inevitable," said rebel Democrat Chan Choi-hi.
"I feel we should give it a try," he told a news conference. He said he had no plan to quit the party, but a party leader immediately signalled there would be trouble.
Party vice-chairman Yeung Sum told reporters the party's committee would meet to decide how to discipline Chan. "He should know what our position is," Yeung said. "It's unethical."
The Democratic Party, Hong Kong's largest, virulently opposes the provisional legislature as China's way to snuff out democracy in the British colony after the handover on July 1.
China, upset by electoral reforms in Hong Kong, has vowed to scrap the present elected Legislative Council and replace it with the provisional body until new elections in 1998.

On Monday, another pro-democracy party with a pivotal role in the present assembly, the Association for Democracy and People's Livelihood, suffered a major split when 16 of its members quit because of its decision to chase seats in the new body.

The 60 members of the interim body will be chosen on December 21 by a 400-strong Selection Committee formed under China's close supervision. The same body is also choosing Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader. The public have no say in either process.
More than 106 pro-China politicans and former lawmakers have collected application forms for the new legislature seats since the three-week registration period began on Monday.
